name: Search bar
statusNote: New maximum width, centered-text style, and a "contained" full-screen expansion where the collapsed bar persists visually inside the expanded view are new in Expressive.
summary: A persistent, pill-shaped entry point for search that expands into a full-screen or docked search view showing suggestions/results. Use the compact bar wherever search is a secondary action in a screen's app bar; the expanded view is a transient state of the same control, not a separate screen the user navigates to.

inputs.name: inputField
inputs.description: The text input row: leading icon, input/hint text, optional trailing icon/avatar.

inputs.name: expanded
inputs.description: Whether the search view is showing. The caller owns it.

inputs.name: onExpandedChange
inputs.description: Called with the new expanded value when the bar or its scrim is activated/dismissed.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The results/suggestions container shown below the header once expanded.

inputs.name: presentation
inputs.description: full-screen replaces the screen; full-screen-contained (Expressive) keeps the collapsed bar's shape/position as the header with no divider; docked expands into a bounded popup anchored under the bar; docked-with-gap adds a gap and its own scrim/dropdown shape between the bar and the popup.

inputs.name: onSearch
inputs.description: Input field: runs a search for the current query text.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Input field: hint content shown when the query is empty.

inputs.name: leadingIcon
inputs.description: Input field: leading icon, e.g. search glyph, menu, or back.

inputs.name: trailingIcon
inputs.description: Input field: trailing icon or avatar.

anatomy.name: Collapsed input field
anatomy.description: The pill-shaped bar: leading icon, input/hint text, optional trailing icon/avatar.

anatomy.name: Expanded header
anatomy.description: The input row inside the expanded view, either docked or full-screen height.

anatomy.name: Divider
anatomy.description: Separates the header from results in the expanded view.

anatomy.name: Scrim
anatomy.description: Full-screen only: dims content behind the expanded view during the transition.

variants.description: Expands into a new full-screen surface; the collapsed bar does not persist visually.
Expressive: expands full-screen but the collapsed bar's shape/position persists as the header, no divider.
Expands into a bounded popup anchored under the bar (tablets/desktop).

layout.text: Collapsed width is clamped between 360dp and 720dp — the Expressive "new maximum width" the MDC docs call out.
Vertical padding inside the collapsed bar is a fixed 8dp above and below the input row, independent of the bar's container-height token.
Icon-to-edge padding in the search bar is 16dp, vs. 12dp in a generic text field.

Full-screen expanded header height comes from the full-screen header token; docked expanded header height from the docked header token. Top padding above the header shrinks from the collapsed bar's padding to 0 as the expansion progresses.
Docked expanded results table has a minimum height of 240dp and caps at 2/3 of screen height standalone, or 1/2 when shown with a gap under the bar.

states.text: State is modeled as a discrete Collapsed/Expanded value plus a continuous progress float driving the transition — implementors should expose both a discrete state and an interpolation value, not just a boolean.

states.label: shape-morph
states.text: The collapsed pill interpolates its corner radius down to 0 as progress goes to 1, becoming the full-screen container's rectangle shape only once fully expanded (only when the bar uses the default collapsed shape); for the docked variant the target shape is the docked container shape instead. Width/height also lerp from the collapsed bar's measured bounds to the container's full constraints over the same progress.

states.label: full-screen-motion
states.text: Full-screen expand uses a slow-spatial spring, collapse uses a default-spatial spring.

states.label: contained-full-screen-motion
states.text: Contained full-screen (Expressive) uses a fast-spatial spring for both expand and collapse.

states.label: docked-with-gap-motion
states.text: Docked-with-gap expand uses a default-spatial spring, collapse uses a fast-spatial spring; the results content fade-in/out inside the contained/gap variants animates separately from the container's spatial spring.

states.label: predictive-back
states.text: While a system back gesture is in progress, the expanded surface previews collapsing by scaling down to 0.9 of its size, offset by up to 24dp vertically and 1/20 of width horizontally, clamped to an 8dp margin from the edge; releasing/committing the gesture finishes the normal collapse transition.

behaviour.text: The keyboard is dismissed automatically once the bar reaches the collapsed state, not on expand-start.
When embedded in a top app bar with a scroll behavior, the bar's container/app-bar colors cross-fade based on the scroll-overlap fraction, independent of the expand/collapse transition.

Treat "compact bar" and "search view" as two rendered states of one state machine, not two components — the shape/size morph requires interpolating between the collapsed bar's measured bounds and the expanded container's bounds every frame of the transition, not swapping components at a threshold.

keyboard: Escape or the back gesture collapses the expanded view.
semantics: The collapsed bar behaves as a search entry point (role search/button); activating it moves focus to the expanded input field.
The expanded full-screen view is presented as a modal surface (dialog semantics) — back/escape must collapse it; the docked variant is a dismissible popup instead.
Minimum touch target on leading/trailing icons follows the platform minimum, independent of the avatar-size/icon-size tokens which describe the glyph, not the hit area.

notes.text: The Expressive "contained" variant's header keeps the collapsed bar's shape and drops the header/results divider, so the input field visually reads as "the same bar, now docked at the top" rather than a new surface appearing.
Full-screen and docked variants use different max-height ratios for their results area — don't share one clamp constant between them.
